input.rationale: Convert part of the snapshot-restore refutation into a measurement. The earlier account relied on raft.restore's stale check and on the log restore setting the committed position; this execution delivers an out-of-date snapshot and a newer one to a follower through its real handler. Local construction runs showed the stale snapshot exposed no snapshot and left the commit at 4, while the newer snapshot was exposed at index 10 and advanced the commit to 10. Membership replacement remains source-only and is recorded as such.

scope.description: Snapshot admission at a follower. A follower that has committed index 4 receives an out-of-date snapshot at index 3 and then a newer snapshot at index 10; the snapshot exposed by its update and its committed index are recorded after each delivery.
assumptions: Three real in-process Raft Peer handlers bootstrap membership {1,2,3}, node 1 leads, and node 2 has committed index 4 after the leader's no-op; each node uses a test-only in-memory ILogDB.
Both snapshots carry the current voter membership, so the role-map replacement path is a no-op in this case and only the log and commit effects are measured.
The snapshots are delivered as InstallSnapshot messages through the follower's real handler, with indexes 3 and 10 and terms 1 and 2.
The follower's committed index is read from the harness's tracked commit, which advances only when an update reports a higher commit.
Production code is unchanged.
excluded: The case does not exercise membership replacement, the state machine Recover task, or a restart.
No transport or persistence path is exercised.
Snapshot corruption and operator-supplied snapshots are excluded.

experiment.prefix: The harness launches three real Raft peers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and ticks node 1 until its current-term no-op is committed, leaving node 2 at committed index 4. It delivers an InstallSnapshot at index 3 to node 2, pumps its update, and records whether a snapshot is exposed and the follower's committed index. It then delivers an InstallSnapshot at index 10, pumps the update, and records the exposed snapshot index and the committed index.
experiment.requirement: A follower must reject a snapshot whose index does not exceed its committed index and must accept a newer one, exposing it for application and advancing its committed index to the snapshot index without moving it backward.
experiment.responsibility: raft.restore owns the index and role guards and delegates to the log restore, which sets the committed and processed positions. The experiment exercises those real paths on a follower and changes only the snapshot index.

comparisons.description: An out-of-date snapshot must not be exposed for application.
The committed index must not move when an out-of-date snapshot is rejected.
The newer snapshot must be exposed at its own index.
Accepting the newer snapshot must advance the committed index to the snapshot index.

scope.description: Three in-process Raft peers with real Peer handlers and a test-only in-memory ILogDB. Nodes 2 and 3 issue ReadIndex requests with distinct SystemCtx values; the later context is confirmed first and the resulting reply for node 2 is routed through node 2's real follower handler and pendingReadIndex consumer.
assumptions: The three peers bootstrap membership {1,2,3}; node 1 is ticked until its current-term no-op commits.
The in-memory ILogDB preserves the ILogDB methods and indices needed for bootstrap, replication, and term lookup; it does not model disk failure, restart, or snapshots.

Both ReadIndex requests are queued at leader 1 before either heartbeat response is delivered. The later heartbeat is delivered to node 3 first, while the earlier heartbeat to node 2 is withheld. This is a controlled but ordinary reordering of same-term heartbeat responses.
The applied index for the pending batch is taken from the ReadyToRead produced by node 2's real follower handler, not invented.

No production code is modified. The client timeout is not waited for; completion is checked synchronously after applying the returned ready index, and the source pending-read timeout path remains the eventual endpoint.
excluded: No claim about every transport schedule, malicious peers, disk faults, snapshot restoration, witnesses, or observer-initiated reads.
No claim that every ReadIndex request times out; this probe concerns the demonstrated earlier-request/later-confirmation ordering.

scope.description: Logical-deadline case in the same three-peer in-process harness. A later context is confirmed first, node 2 receives the wrong context, its applied ReadyToRead leaves the original batch at index zero, and the pending-read clock is advanced past the caller's deadline.

excluded: This case measures the logical deadline and GC path, not real wall-clock scheduling or transport delay.

basis.prefix: The harness launches three real Raft peers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and ticks node 1 until its current-term no-op is committed. Node 2 and node 3 each register a node-level pending read under a generated context and forward it to the leader through the real follower path, so both requests sit in the leader's readIndex queue. The harness then calls Tick once on the leader and pumps it; the produced heartbeat addressed to node 3 carries the newest queued context. The node-level pendingReadIndex registers one observer read under a generated context A and the observer peer forwards it to the leader. A later voter-originated request with context B is queued, node 3 receives its heartbeat and returns the confirmation that the leader uses to confirm B, and the leader's reply addressed to observer 4 is emitted and then handled by the observer peer. The resulting ReadyToRead output is fed to pendingReadIndex.addReady and the reply's log index to pendingReadIndex.applied, and the run records the ready index, whether the batch keyed by context A still exists and its index, and whether the client read completed. A late confirmation of context A is then delivered and checked for a context-correct reply. The control case repeats the setup, confirms context A first, and records the same completion fields.

scope.description: Admission of ReadIndex confirmations. A leader with voters {1,2,3} queues one follower read and then receives the same confirming heartbeat response twice from node 4, which is in no role map, once through the Peer admission path and once directly at the raft state machine; a response from voter 3 follows.
assumptions: The leader is a real raft state machine built by the package test helper with committed membership {1,2,3} and a committed no-op in its current term.
Node 4 is absent from the leader's remotes, observers and witnesses maps, which is the state left by any transition that removed it from every role.
The Peer admission path and the raft state machine are both exercised with the same response, so each layer is measured separately.
The confirming responses carry the queued context in Hint and HintHigh and are delivered with a zero term, as heartbeat responses are.
Production code is unchanged.
excluded: The case does not execute a configuration change; it starts from the post-transition role maps directly.
No transport, persistence or restart path is exercised.
A forged response from a node that is still a current voter is not covered.

basis.prefix: The harness builds a leader for voters {1,2,3}, commits a current-term no-op, queues one ReadIndex request from node 2 under context {101,1002}, and records the queue length. It then delivers a HeartbeatResp carrying that context from node 4 through a Peer value, records the queue length and emitted replies, and repeats the same delivery directly at the raft state machine to bypass the Peer filter. Finally it delivers the same response from voter 3 through the Peer and records the queue length and the number of ReadIndex replies addressed to node 2.
basis.requirement: A ReadIndex confirmation must count only responses from nodes the leader currently admits in its role maps: a response from a node absent from every role map must leave the pending request unconfirmed, while a current voter's response must confirm it.
basis.responsibility: Peer.Handle filters response messages from senders outside the role maps, and the leader's remote lookup in lw resolves the responding remote before handleLeaderHeartbeatResp can pass the hint to readIndex.confirm. The experiment exercises those real layers and changes only which sender supplies the response.

comparisons.description: A response from a node outside every role map, delivered through the Peer, must not change the pending queue.
The same response handed straight to the raft state machine must also leave the pending queue unchanged.
A current voter's response must confirm the queued context and produce a reply for the requester.

scope.description: Confirmation after a live removal. Voters 1 and 2 apply a RemoveNode config change for node 3, a ReadIndex request from node 2 is queued at the leader, and the confirming heartbeat response is delivered first from removed node 3 and then from current voter 2.
assumptions: Three real in-process Raft Peer handlers bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and node 1 is leader with a committed current-term no-op; each node uses a test-only in-memory ILogDB.
The removal is applied through Peer.ApplyConfigChange on the two remaining voters, which is the call the surrounding node makes when it applies a committed RemoveNode entry.
The confirming responses carry the queued context and arrive with a zero term, as heartbeat responses do; they are delivered through the real Peer admission path used for network messages.
Production code is unchanged.
excluded: Node 3 does not run the removal itself; only the remaining voters' maps are updated, which is the leader-side state that decides admissions.
No transport, persistence or restart path is exercised.
The direct-to-raft admission layer is covered by a separate receipt for an unknown sender; this case exercises the Peer layer only.

basis.prefix: The harness launches three real Raft peers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and ticks node 1 until its current-term no-op is committed. Both remaining voters then apply a RemoveNode config change for node 3 and pump their updates, and the run records that the voter set is now {1,2}. Node 2 forwards a ReadIndex request carrying context {303,3003} to the leader. A HeartbeatResp carrying that context from node 3 is delivered to the leader and the run records how many ReadIndex replies addressed to node 2 it produced; the same response is then delivered from voter 2 and the reply count is recorded again.
basis.requirement: After a node is removed from the voter set, a delayed heartbeat response from that node must not satisfy the ReadIndex quorum, while a response from a current voter must confirm the request.
basis.responsibility: The applied RemoveNode path deletes the node from the raft role maps, Peer.Handle admits response messages only from senders in those maps, and readIndex.confirm confirms only when enough admitted responses arrive. The experiment exercises those real paths and changes only which node answers.

comparisons.description: A response from the removed node must not confirm the queued read.
A response from a current voter must confirm the queued read and produce a reply.

scope.description: Proposal gate at a live leader. A leader for voters {1,2,3} proposes an AddNode for node 4 and then, without committing or applying it, proposes an AddNode for node 5; the saved entries and the dropped-entry reports of both updates are recorded.
assumptions: Three real in-process Raft Peer handlers bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and node 1 is leader with a committed current-term no-op; each node uses a test-only in-memory ILogDB.

Both configuration changes are submitted through Peer.ProposeConfigChange, which enters the leader's proposal handler; no follower acknowledgement is delivered, so the first proposal stays uncommitted and unapplied.
The leader's update is inspected directly, so saved entry types and the dropped-entry report are the measured endpoints.
The surrounding node would apply a committed configuration change through ApplyConfigChange, which is not reached here.
Production code is unchanged.
excluded: The case does not commit or apply either change, so it measures the proposal gate only.
No transport, persistence or restart path is exercised.
The leadership-recovery check and the election gate are covered by source only.

basis.prefix: The harness launches three real Raft peers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and ticks node 1 until its current-term no-op is committed. It proposes an AddNode config change for node 4 with key 9001 through the leader peer and records the update: how many configuration-change entries were saved and how many entries were reported dropped. Without delivering any acknowledgement it then proposes an AddNode config change for node 5 with key 9002 and records the same fields plus the key of any dropped entry and how many plain application entries were saved in place of the configuration change.
basis.requirement: While a configuration change is pending, the leader must not append a second configuration-change entry that could later be committed with the same quorum; a second proposal must be reported dropped and must not become a configuration-change entry.
basis.responsibility: handleLeaderPropose inspects each proposed entry, replaces a configuration change with an empty application entry and reports it dropped when the pending flag is set. The experiment exercises that handler through the real leader peer and changes only whether the first change has been applied.

comparisons.description: The first proposal must be saved as a configuration-change entry.
The second proposal must not be saved as a configuration-change entry while the first is pending.
The second proposal must be reported dropped under its own key.

scope.description: Snapshot admission at a follower. A follower that has committed index 4 receives an out-of-date snapshot at index 3 and then a newer snapshot at index 10; the snapshot exposed by its update and its committed index are recorded after each delivery.
assumptions: Three real in-process Raft Peer handlers bootstrap membership {1,2,3}, node 1 leads, and node 2 has committed index 4 after the leader's no-op; each node uses a test-only in-memory ILogDB.
Both snapshots carry the current voter membership, so the role-map replacement path is a no-op in this case and only the log and commit effects are measured.
The snapshots are delivered as InstallSnapshot messages through the follower's real handler, with indexes 3 and 10 and terms 1 and 2.
The follower's committed index is read from the harness's tracked commit, which advances only when an update reports a higher commit.
Production code is unchanged.
excluded: The case does not exercise membership replacement, the state machine Recover task, or a restart.
No transport or persistence path is exercised.
Snapshot corruption and operator-supplied snapshots are excluded.

basis.prefix: The harness launches three real Raft peers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and ticks node 1 until its current-term no-op is committed, leaving node 2 at committed index 4. It delivers an InstallSnapshot at index 3 to node 2, pumps its update, and records whether a snapshot is exposed and the follower's committed index. It then delivers an InstallSnapshot at index 10, pumps the update, and records the exposed snapshot index and the committed index.
basis.requirement: A follower must reject a snapshot whose index does not exceed its committed index and must accept a newer one, exposing it for application and advancing its committed index to the snapshot index without moving it backward.
basis.responsibility: raft.restore owns the index and role guards and delegates to the log restore, which sets the committed and processed positions. The experiment exercises those real paths on a follower and changes only the snapshot index.

comparisons.description: An out-of-date snapshot must not be exposed for application.
The committed index must not move when an out-of-date snapshot is rejected.
The newer snapshot must be exposed at its own index.
Accepting the newer snapshot must advance the committed index to the snapshot index.
